items.q: Is it cheaper to paint or replace kitchen cabinets?

a.text: Painting is dramatically cheaper — typically $3,000 to $7,000 for a standard kitchen versus $15,000 to $40,000+ for replacement. For most kitchens, painting delivers the large majority of the visual change at a fraction of the cost and in about a week instead of a month.

a.text: The honest qualifier: painting only makes sense if the boxes are structurally sound. If doors are delaminating, boxes are sagging, particleboard has swollen from water damage, or the layout itself does not work, paint is money spent on a problem it cannot fix. Solid wood, plywood, and sound MDF doors take paint extremely well. We will tell you during the walkthrough which situation you are in, including when the answer is that you should replace rather than hire us.

items.q: Is professional cabinet painting worth it, or can I do it myself?

a.text: Cabinets are the single hardest interior painting job to do well, and the gap between a professional and a DIY result is more visible than on any other surface. Cabinets get touched constantly, sit at eye level, and show every brush mark under kitchen lighting.
a.html: Cabinets are the single hardest interior painting job to do well, and the gap between a professional and a DIY result is more visible than on any other surface. Cabinets get touched constantly, sit at eye level, and show every brush mark under kitchen lighting.

a.text: The difference is method rather than skill alone. A professional cabinet finish means full degreasing, de-glossing or sanding, a bonding primer specified for the substrate, and sprayed topcoats in a controlled setup — usually with doors removed, labeled, and finished off-site on racks. Brushing and rolling cabinets leaves texture that reads as amateur immediately, and skipping the degreasing step on a kitchen means the finish will peel at the handles within a year no matter how good the paint was.

items.q: What is the downside to painting kitchen cabinets?

a.text: Three real ones, and any contractor who tells you there are none is selling. First, painted cabinets are less forgiving of impact than stained wood — chips show as a bright spot rather than blending, though touch-up is straightforward if you keep the leftover paint. Second, the process takes about a week during which your kitchen is partly out of service. Third, it is not reversible in practice; returning to natural wood later means stripping, which is expensive and rarely fully successful.
a.html: Three real ones, and any contractor who tells you there are none is selling. First, painted cabinets are less forgiving of impact than stained wood — chips show as a bright spot rather than blending, though touch-up is straightforward if you keep the leftover paint. Second, the process takes about a week during which your kitchen is partly out of service. Third, it is not reversible in practice; returning to natural wood later means stripping, which is expensive and rarely fully successful.

a.text: What is not a real downside, if the work is done properly: durability. A correctly prepped and sprayed cabinet finish holds up for years of daily use. Nearly every horror story about peeling cabinets traces back to skipped degreasing or a primer that was never specified for the substrate.

items.q: How much does Home Depot charge to paint kitchen cabinets?

a.text: Big-box cabinet refinishing programs generally quote $4,000 to $10,000 for a standard kitchen. The work is subcontracted to a third-party crew rather than performed by the retailer. [Include link]
a.html: Big-box cabinet refinishing programs generally quote $4,000 to $10,000 for a standard kitchen. The work is subcontracted to a third-party crew rather than performed by the retailer. [Include link]

a.text: The thing worth comparing is not the headline price but who stands behind the finish and what the process actually is. Ask any bidder — including us — three questions: are doors removed and sprayed, or finished in place with a brush? What primer is specified, and why that one for these cabinets? Who honors the warranty in two years, the retailer or the sub? The answers separate the bids far more reliably than the number does.

items.q: How long does cabinet painting take, and can I use my kitchen?

a.text: Six to eight working days for a typical kitchen. Day one is removal, labeling, and degreasing; the middle days are prep and spray on doors and drawer fronts while boxes are finished in place; the final day is reinstallation and hardware.
